title: FDA Drug Safety Communication: Possible increased risk of fractures of the hip, wrist, and spine with the use of proton pump inhibitors
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety Communication, 25 May 2010, updated 23 March 2011
result: Review of seven published epidemiological studies using claims databases: six reported an increased risk of hip, wrist or spine fracture with PPI use, greatest with high doses or use for one year or more, mainly in people aged 50 years or older. The databases lacked data on family history of osteoporosis, smoking, weight, height, alcohol, calcium and vitamin D intake, indication and falls. Randomised trials, generally six months long, found no increase in fractures. It is not clear whether PPI use causes the increased risk. The 2011 update judged fracture risk with short-term, low-dose use unlikely.
